claims.statement: GPT-OSS-Lite implements attention with 8 query heads and 4 key/value heads at head_dim 96; a fused KV projection produces the compact K/V tensors, and repeat_kv expands each KV head to two query heads before SDPA.

Attention layer mode is fixed by layer parity: even-indexed layers are sliding-window layers using the configured window, while odd-indexed layers are full causal layers; the production configuration has 12 layers and window_size 128.

The alternating SWA/full schedule is the basis of the mixed KV-cache reduction: windowed layers retain at most the window in ring buffers while global layers retain the complete prefix, yielding the benchmark's approximately 1.94x reduction at 4K and 2.00x reduction at 128K versus all-full storage.

The causal_attention production entrypoint routes attention through PyTorch scaled_dot_product_attention: square full attention without a sink uses is_causal=True, while rectangular, windowed, and sink cases use explicit additive masks or an extended sink-column representation.

Attention masks constrain visibility but the current implementation does not automatically provide sparse FLOP reduction: the manual oracle explicitly forms an O(T²) score matrix, and masked SDPA backend selection remains dependent on PyTorch heuristics rather than a repository-selected block-sparse kernel.

A learned sink is one per-head logit represented as an extra zero key/value column. Its probability participates in softmax normalization but contributes no value, allowing attention mass to be absorbed without occupying a KV-cache slot.
Sink bias is clamped only at forward use to [-10.0, 15.0]; the raw nn.Parameter is not mutated and remains connected to autograd, while generation can cache the clamped tensor per attention layer.

Because SDPA float masks are additive, allowed real-key positions must receive 0.0 and forbidden positions true -inf; casting an allowed/forbidden boolean mask directly to a float would leave blocked positions visible and can leak future tokens.

GPT-OSS-Lite applies YaRN RoPE to Q and K before GQA repetition, using a 48-pair table for head_dim 96; production settings extend a 4096-token original span to a 131072-token target with scale_factor 32 and optional mscale.

YaRN blends base inverse frequencies with frequencies divided by the scale factor across a clamped linear ramp; compute_yarn_mscale returns 1.0 for scale_factor <= 1 and otherwise 0.1*log(scale_factor)+1, and the module stores inv_freq as a non-persistent buffer.

YaRN does not silently accept a degenerate ramp: when high <= low, compute_yarn_freqs emits a UserWarning and uses a zero ramp identity fallback; odd head dimensions and non-positive sequence lengths raise ValueError.

Global layers optionally prune the leading head_dim//4 RoPE pair columns after YaRN scaling by overwriting them with exactly cos=1.0 and sin=0.0, while windowed layers retain all pairs; for the production head_dim this is 24 pair columns.

Cached decoding rotates the new query and fresh key, stores the rotated key, retrieves chronological cached K/V, and applies attention with a one-query rectangular alignment; windowed caches use ring-buffer rollover while global caches grow and retain the full prefix.

The manual attention implementation is the correctness oracle: it explicitly upcasts Q and K before score matmul for FP32 score accumulation, applies causal/window masks, adds the sink logit column when requested, and strips the sink column before multiplying by V.
Router-related FP32 softmax stability is a separate MoE contract from attention score accumulation and sink handling.
